raw_response:
My family has 8 mu of land here in Quzhou. My husband goes to work in the city some months, so I handle the farm myself most of the time. I have been doing this since I was in my twenties. I know this land.

There is no question about what I grow — winter wheat and summer corn, one after the other, on the same 7 mu. Everyone here does this. The soil is good for it, the water is manageable, and I know exactly what to do at every stage. I have done it hundreds of times. I do not experiment with unfamiliar crops when this rotation feeds the family and gives us cash income.

For wheat, I plant in early October, right after the corn comes off. I buy improved seed from the seed shop in the county town — same variety as the past two years, it did well. I rotary till after the corn to chop up the stalks and prepare the seedbed. I put down compound fertilizer as base fertilizer at planting, then top-dress with urea in early spring at jointing. I irrigate three times: before the ground freezes in November, at jointing in April, and at heading in May. The groundwater here is reliable. I spray herbicide in autumn and fungicide once in spring — powdery mildew and rust are the main worries.

For corn, I plant right after wheat harvest in June. No tillage — I seed directly into the stubble. That saves me work and fuel money. I always buy hybrid seed, that is just how it is done now. Summer rains here are usually enough, so I irrigate only once if July is dry. I spray pre-emergence herbicide at planting and check for corn borer once in summer.

I also keep 1 mu near the house for vegetables — cabbage, yard-long beans, maybe some garlic — partly for the family, partly to sell a little at the township market. Nothing large.
